bug_semantics: A platform-user with a network role could call GET /api/extclients/{network} and receive every ExtClient object, whose JSON representation included the WireGuard privatekey field; a later host-read grant also made GET /api/nodes/{network} return node records containing StaticNode.PrivateKey. UI ownership filtering did not protect these API responses.
flaw_origin: Commit cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638 activated the previously declared platform-user role by inserting PlatformUserUserPermissionTemplate during UserRolesInit. That made GetRole succeed for platform users and allowed their network roles to reach an already-existing all-extclients Read scope and unredacted list response. Its parent did not register that role. Commit 996410fc61f0f807b6b12d506ea1ac878e0f84c6 later added all-host Read permission to network users, expanding the same secret-return problem to /api/nodes/{network}, but the advisory-class exposure already existed through /api/extclients/{network} after cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638 shows human author and committer abhishek9686 <abhi281342@gmail.com> and message 'add platform user to default role', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: Bundle advisory GHSA-4hgg-c4rr-6h7f / CVE-2026-29196 states that a platform-user with network access can retrieve all WireGuard private keys through GET /api/extclients/{network} or GET /api/nodes/{network}; CVE.org record CVE-2026-29196 is PUBLISHED, not rejected or withdrawn.

At cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638, controllers/ext_client.go getNetworkExtClients calls GetNetworkExtClients(network) and directly json-encodes the complete slice, while models/extclient.go exposes PrivateKey as json:"privatekey".

git show cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638 -- logic/user_mgmt.go adds exactly the json.Marshal and database.Insert calls for PlatformUserUserPermissionTemplate in UserRolesInit; git show 76dda15a310c22f253f720d3c87104c6e5fcdd1a:logic/user_mgmt.go confirms those registration calls are absent in the immediate parent, so the platform-user role could not pass GetRole there.

The BIC tree already contains NetworkUserPermissionTemplate with Read access to models.AllExtClientsRsrcID, and the list route has no target resource ID or response redaction; therefore activating platform-user makes the full list reachable without per-owner enforcement.

git show 996410fc61f0f807b6b12d506ea1ac878e0f84c6 -- pro/logic/user_mgmt.go adds Read access to models.AllHostRsrcID for network users; its parent lacks that grant, establishing the later /api/nodes/{network} expansion independently.

git show 5617d97ce616362e16b6d5e9e9b3cc63f0ac2845 changes controllers/ext_client.go to filter list results with IsUserAllowedAccessToExtClient and blank ExtClient.PrivateKey, and changes controllers/node.go to blank apiNodes[i].StaticNode.PrivateKey before JSON encoding; its parent c23a7b9ea1b6e1db5bfed7697826c440e4c3b2ec still directly encodes both record types.

git tag --contains cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638 includes v1.5.0, proving the BIC predates the affected boundary. git tag --contains 5617d97ce616362e16b6d5e9e9b3cc63f0ac2845 includes v1.5.1 and v1.6.0 but not v1.5.0; the local v1.5.0 tag still has unredacted handlers, so the advisory's claimed v1.5.0 patched boundary is inconsistent with public tag topology, while v1.5.1 contains the direct fix.

git cat-file commit cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638 shows a single-parent non-merge commit authored and committed by abhishek9686 with no AI-related trailer or bot identity; no squash decomposition is needed.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and the CVE record is published. The extclients path is the earliest complete advisory mechanism: the endpoint and secret-bearing JSON model already existed, but platform-user was only a declaration until cb940ac68466156e63c39172c5e85f8fc9600638 inserted the role into the runtime role store. With that activation, a platform-user carrying the existing network-user role passed NetworkPermissionsCheck and its all-extclients Read permission, while list requests had no resource ID on which the ownership check could operate, so the handler returned other users' private keys. Direct inspection of parent 76dda15a310c22f253f720d3c87104c6e5fcdd1a proves the activation calls absent. The nodes alternative was added later by 996410fc61f0f807b6b12d506ea1ac878e0f84c6 and does not supersede the earlier BIC because the extclients route was already sufficient. Commit 5617d97ce616362e16b6d5e9e9b3cc63f0ac2845 directly closes both paths by owner-filtering extclients and redacting private keys from both response types. Public tag topology places that fix in v1.5.1 rather than the advisory-stated v1.5.0, a release-metadata discrepancy that does not change the causal BIC or its authorship. Because the exact BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no AI marker, the verdict is NOT_AI.
